## [Encoder optimization pass](ROADMAP.md#encoder-optimization-pass) `@jpegxl-rs.track.encoder-optimization/1`

### Native Windows equivalents for the last bash-only quality/conformance tooling (cjxl-match, fetch-conformance)

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.work.native-windows-quality-tooling/1` · part of `@jpegxl-rs.track.encoder-optimization/1`

Native Windows encoding is materially faster than WSL, and the user asked that any tester script or binary lacking a Windows equivalent be built for Windows. The standing quality loop and corpus setup had two remaining bash-only entry points: cjxl-match.sh (the cjxl -e7 matched-byte comparator that feeds summarise.py's 'cjxl at matched bytes' table) and the tracked tools/fetch-conformance.sh (pinned corpus clone). Add faithful PowerShell ports — cjxl-match.ps1 (gitignored scratch, beside its siblings) and tools/fetch-conformance.ps1 (tracked) — using the Windows oracle binaries, no awk/wslpath/WSL, keeping the fetch pin in lockstep with the .sh, and point the tracked docs and local harness README at the native equivalents. Do not change any codec code, preset, or output.
